title: thymus serpyllum f. braunii
intro: Thymus serpyllum f. braunii, commonly known as wild thyme, is a subspecies of the Thymus serpyllum species, a low-growing, perennial herb native to Europe and Western Asia. It is valued for its numerous health benefits, including its antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties, which can help to boost the immune system, reduce stress and anxiety, and protect against oxidative damage. The therapeutic actions of wild thyme include its ability to act as an expectorant, relieving respiratory issues such as coughs and congestion, as well as its antiseptic and antiviral properties, making it useful for wound healing and preventing infections. Wild thyme contains bioactive constituents such as thymol, carvacrol, and ursolic acid, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and have been shown to have potential anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory effects.
